# `jouet edit replace`

- **Usage:** `jouet edit replace [FLAGS] [PATHS]…`

Replace text in files, given on the command line

Matches anywhere in a file, like `str::replace`, and requires exactly one match in each file unless --count or --all says otherwise. Repeat --old and --new for several replacements: the Nth --new replaces the Nth --old, in order. Every replacement applies to every file, and every file is checked before any is written, so a rename across files is one call that lands whole or not at all.

Examples:
  jouet edit replace src/lib.rs --old 'let x = 1;' --new 'let x = 2;'
  jouet edit replace a.py b.py --old retry_limit --new max_attempts --all
  jouet edit replace app.py --old 'a()' --new 'b()' --old 'c()' --new 'd()'

## Arguments
- **`[PATHS]…`** — The files to edit

## Flags
- **`--old <TEXT>`** — The text to find. Repeatable. It may start with `-`, such as a Markdown list item
- **`--new <TEXT>`** — The text to put in its place, one for each --old. It may start with `-` too
- **`--count <N>`** — How many matches each --old must have in each file
- **`--all`** — Replace every match (at least one in each file)
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
